ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a two-stage transistor amplifier circuit. The collector of the transistor on the right is connected to +Ucc through Rc2, and is connected to uo through the output coupling capacitor. The branch labeled Rf and Cf is located at the upper/middle part of the right-side stage, forming a feedback branch from the collector output node of the transistor on the right back to the base input node of the transistor on the right. Reasoning: This branch samples from the output-end collector, therefore it belongs to voltage feedback; the feedback signal is connected in parallel to the input base node, therefore it is shunt feedback; the branch contains capacitor Cf, mainly playing a feedback role for AC signals, therefore it is AC feedback; the transistor on the right is a common-emitter amplifier stage, the collector output and base input are inverted in phase, and after the feedback returns to the input end it weakens the original input action, therefore it is negative feedback; moreover the feedback forms around the same right-side stage, so it is local-stage feedback.
